- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 80), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap forecast decline to 5–7% below peak for 3–7 days.
- If sentiment turns negative after a peak, model often fails to adjust downward fast enough; apply a 2–4 day lag correction with gradual downward slope.
- Mean reversion is stronger in 30-day horizon; if forecast is > 10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.33/1.00 alternation, model tends to misread momentum; use 3-day moving average of sentiment to smooth forecast bias.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently 2–4% below model, apply a 1–2% downward bias correction for next 7 days unless sentiment turns positive.
